rationale: A rank-product of two textbook anomalies (operating profitability and total accruals) is effectively log-additive rather than the sharp conjunctive "AND" claimed, so it is close to a trivial composite score of two known effects and overlaps heavily with published cash-based profitability.

Internally consistent and the absolute-accrual reliability penalty is a defensible twist, but note the mechanical piecewise structure — for positive-accrual firms the signal collapses exactly to oancf/at (known cash-flow profitability), so much of the variation is a rediscovery in disguise.

The state-dependent test is coherent and matches the hypothesis, but the 0/1 gate parks roughly half the universe at exactly zero, creating a large mass point that will distort quantile breakpoints and make the short leg consist only of cash-confirmed low-margin firms — the portfolio evidence should be interpreted with that composition caveat.

The worst-accrual-year (TS_MAX) framing is a genuinely different measurement of accounting stretch than level accruals and the expression matches the stated hypothesis, though it remains a rank-product blend of two known themes and the three-period history will cost coverage.

Grading profitability by accrual-process instability is economically distinct from the signed-accrual anomaly and the sign logic is consistent, but accrual/earnings volatility is itself a documented earnings-quality anomaly and the five-period VOL window will materially shrink coverage, so the incremental interaction must be shown to survive controls for each leg.

This is essentially a direct rediscovery of Ball–Gerakos–Linnainmaa–Nikolaev cash-based operating profitability (gross profit less working-capital accruals scaled by assets), and the one-year DELTA of a level makes it a noisy single-period variant of that published measure rather than a new mechanism.
